Magkasamang ininspeksiyon nina Metropolitan Manila Development Authority Chairman Atty. Don Artes at Senador Raffy Tulfo ang MMDA Communications and Command Center sa punong tanggapan ng ahensiya sa Pasig City upang maipakita sa mambabatas ang proseso ng implementasyon ng No Contact Apprehension Policy (NCAP) at paggamit ng body-worn cameras ng mga traffic enforcer.

Sa naturang pagbisita, ipinirisinta ni Atty. Artes ang real-time traffic monitoring system at ang paggamit ng mga body-worn cameras ng Swift Traffic Action Group (STAG) enforcers na pinapangunahan ni Edison "Bong" Nebrija. Ayon kay Artes, nananatiling pangunahing layunin ng ahensiya ang modernisasyon ng traffic enforcement upang patas, maayos, at ligtas ang operasyon para sa mga motorista at traffic enforcers.

"Kahit yung mga body-cam natin, ginagamit na natin sa panghuhuli para wala nang masyadong interaction, wala nang pagtatalo," dagdag ni Chairman Artes.

Binigyang-diin naman ni Senator Tulfo na ang kaniyang pagbisita ay bahagi ng kaniyang pagsusulong ng pagkakaloob ng hazard pay at  regularisasyon para sa mga enforcers at street sweepers sa MMDA.

Layunin ng MMDA na ipagpatuloy ang paggamit ng makabagong teknolohiya at pagsuporta sa kapakanan ng mga kawani habang isinusulong ang mas maayos at ligtas na daloy ng trapiko at pampublikong serbisyo sa Metro Manila.

#mmda

data.raw_text:
Typhoon kills 66 people, with 400,000 displaced, 26 missing in the #Philippines 

At least 66 people were killed and 26 others remained missing after #TyphoonKalmaegi ( locally known as #Tino} struck the Philippines, displacing more than 400,000 people, officials said.

According to the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Council, the death toll rose to 66, including the six involved in Tuesday's helicopter crash during a search-and-rescue operation, local daily The Inquirer reported. 
Most fatalities were reported from Central Visayas, the worst-hit region in the country. 
Central Visayas, located in central Philippines, is an administrative region which includes the provinces of Bohol, Cebu, Negros Oriental, and Siquijor. 

Authorities said that 10 people have been injured in different areas, while more than 1.1 million people have been affected by the severe weather. 

Heavy flooding and landslides have also cut off roads in remote areas, while 52 municipalities continue to experience power outages, authorities said. 

Videos and images in local media showed massive flooding and destruction in several regions in the Philippines, including parts of Cebu province. 

The devastation comes just a month after a powerful 6.9 magnitude earthquake struck northern Cebu, killing many people and displacing thousands. 

Authorities said relief efforts are ongoing, as rescue teams work to reach remote areas cut off by floodwaters and landslides.  
Typhoon Kalmaegi, locally known as Tino, made two landfalls since early Tuesday in the central island of Visayas.  
Tino is expected to leave the Philippine "area of responsibility," monitored by the country's meteorological agency, on Wednesday night or early Thursday morning, while it is expected to regain strength over the South China Sea before heading toward Vietnam, where authorities are preparing for its arrival on Friday.
